questions.stem:
A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis.
At time $t$ seconds, where $t \geqslant 1$
• the displacement of $P$ from $O$ is $x$ metres in the positive $x$ direction, where $x < \frac{1}{2}$
• the velocity of $P$ is $v\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$ in the positive $x$ direction
• the acceleration of $P$ is $a\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$ in the positive $x$ direction
Given that
$$a = 4x-2$$
and that when $t=1$, $x=0$ and $v=1$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Correct method to form a differential equation in $v$ and $x$, separate the variables and integrate to the form $\frac{1}{2}v^2 = Ax^2+Bx\ (+C)$ o.e.
A1: $\left(v\frac{dv}{dx}=4x-2 \Rightarrow\right)$ $\frac{1}{2}v^2 = 2x^2-2x\ (+C)$
A1: $\frac{1}{2}v^2 = 2x^2-2x+\frac{1}{2}$ o.e.
A1: $v = 1-2x$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Method using $v\frac{dv}{dx}$ to form a differential equation in v and x, separate the variables and integrate to the form $\frac{1}{2}v^2 = Ax^2+Bx\ (+C)$ where A and B are non-zero constants. Condone a missing constant of integration. $\int v\,dv$ may be implied by sight of $\frac{1}{2}v^2$. M0 for use of suvat
- A1: A correct equation with or without +C. A1: A fully correct equation including the evaluated constant of integration. A1: Correct only

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
ALT1:
M1: Method to form a differential equation in $x$ and $t$, separate the variables and integrate to the form $D\ln(1-2x)=t\ (+C)$ o.e.
A1: $\left(\int \frac{1}{1-2x}\,dx=\int dt \Rightarrow\right)$ $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1-2x)=t\ (+C)$
A1: $(t=1, x=0 \Rightarrow C=-1)$ $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1-2x)=t-1$ o.e.
dM1: Complete method to obtain $v$ in terms of $t$. For example: $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(v)=t-1\ (+C) \Rightarrow v=\ldots$ in terms of $t$; or $x=\frac{1}{2}(1-e^{2-2t})$ then differentiate wrt $t$ to obtain $v=\ldots$ in terms of $t$
A1: $(v=)e^{2-2t}$
ALT2:
M1: Method to form a differential equation in $v$ and $t$, separate the variables and integrate to the form $\ln v=Et\ (+C)$ o.e.
A1: $\left(\int \frac{1}{v}\,dv=-2\int dt \Rightarrow\right)$ $\ln v=-2t\ (+C)$
A1: $(t=1,v=1 \Rightarrow C=2)$ $\ln(v)=2-2t$ o.e.
dM1: Obtain $v$ in terms of $t$
A1: $v=e^{2-2t}$
Notes: M1 requires method using $v\frac{dv}{dx}$ or $v=\frac{dx}{dt}$ etc, condoning missing constant of integration; M0 for use of suvat throughout. N.B. If the answer to (a) is $v=2x-1$, the maximum score for (b) is M1A1A0M1A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ALT1 A1: Correct equation in x and t, with or without C. N.B. if they start with $v=2x-1$, allow M1A1 for $\frac{1}{2}\ln(2x-1)=t\ (+C)$
- ALT2 M1: $\left\{\frac{dv}{dt}=-2\frac{dx}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dt}=-2v \Rightarrow \ln v=-2t\ (+C)\right\}$ M0 for use of suvat
- ALT2 A1: Correct equation in v and t, with or without C. N.B. if they start with $v=2x-1$, allow M1A1 for $\ln v=Et\ (+C)$
- dM1: Dependent on previous M. A complete method to obtain v as an exponential function in terms of t only. A1: Correct answer only

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hooke's Law to find natural length
parts.reason: This part requires applying Hooke's Law (tension = modulus × extension/natural length) to find L. Elasticity/Hooke's Law is not mentioned anywhere in the M6-M9 statements provided, so this method is not covered.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Horizontal circular motion (conical pendulum) with N2L
parts.reason: This requires setting up equations of motion for uniform circular motion (centripetal acceleration, N2L towards centre) combined with vertical equilibrium. Circular motion is not mentioned in any of the M6-M9 statements (which cover only kinematics in a straight line/2D via vectors, Newton's laws for straight-line/resolved forces, and moments) — no statement covers motion in a circle.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Elastic potential energy (EPE) calculation for elastic strings
parts.reason: This part requires calculating elastic energy stored in a string using the EPE formula (x²/2l), which is nowhere mentioned in the M6-M9 statements (only forces, Newton's laws, kinematics, and moments are covered - no energy methods or elastic strings at all).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Work-energy principle with GPE, KE, EPE and resistance work done
parts.reason: This requires the work-energy principle including GPE, KE and EPE terms, none of which (energy methods, elastic strings) appear in the M6-M9 statements. It also depends on the out-of-spec result from part (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Energy conservation for a particle sliding on a sphere
parts.reason: Uses conservation of energy (GPE to KE) for a particle moving on a curved surface, a mechanics energy method not present in any M6-M9 statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: N2L towards centre of circular path (leaving surface condition) combined with energy
parts.reason: Requires circular motion equations (N2L towards centre, R=0 condition) which are not covered by any M statement, and also depends on the out-of-spec energy result from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Projectile-type motion after leaving a curved surface with energy/circular motion combined
parts.reason: Builds on the circular motion and energy results from (a) and (b) (both out of spec) and requires further use of circular motion energy equations; no statement covers this combination.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Centre of mass of a solid of revolution by integration
parts.reason: Centre of mass is explicitly given as an example topic not covered by any statement (no statement mentions centre of mass, moments of volumes, or integration for centroids), so this is out of spec regardless of the integration technique used.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Centre of mass of composite solid (subtracting hemispheres)
parts.reason: Same reasoning as (a): centre of mass is not covered by any listed statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Equilibrium of a solid resting on its curved surface, using centre of mass position
parts.reason: Depends on the centre of mass results from (a) and (b), which are out of spec, and centre of mass itself is not covered by any statement.

parts.technique: Deriving SHM equation from Hooke's Law and Newton's second law for elastic strings
parts.reason: Simple harmonic motion (SHM) and Hooke's Law/elastic strings are not mentioned in any M6-M9 statement; this is a purely M3-level topic outside the given spec.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Requires the SHM formula v_max = aω, which depends on the SHM result from (a); SHM is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Time interval calculation using SHM displacement/velocity equations
parts.reason: Requires SHM equations for displacement and velocity and depends on the SHM setup in (a)-(b), none of which is covered by any M6-M9 statement.
